notes: Updates land themselves now. When an earlier update had not actually reached the running Kit, the app used to show a screen with a button and otherwise wait; it now quietly reruns the update at the next launch, and only asks you to press the button if that self-heal fails too.

An update waits for your Kit to finish dreaming or reading your history before it restarts anything, so that work is never killed mid-flight. A wait that drags past three hours goes ahead anyway rather than holding your Kit on old code forever.
Each successful update cleans up the images earlier versions left behind. They used to pile up quietly until Docker's disk filled and every later update failed at that same wall.

An update that cannot verify what is running now says exactly that and retries at the next launch. It used to record success on silence, which could leave a Kit convinced it was current while running weeks-old code.

If an update fails, your Kit sends us the error lines from that run, with your sign-in details stripped, so we can fix what went wrong without asking you to dig logs out of your Mac. The beta disclosure at install time names this.

This version renames your Kit's internal containers to say what they are. The updater retires the old ones itself, in the right order, so the swap is clean: your Kit keeps running on the old version until the new one is fully built, and your memories sit in storage that the rename never touches.
